title: Detecting acute pain signals from human EEG
authors: G Sun, Z Wen, D Ok, L Doan, J Wang, Z S Chen et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: source-localized EEG features and sequential state-space pain-onset detection
feature_definition: Unsupervised state-space detector using localized ROI EEG to detect onset of acute pain, compared with SVM.
prediction_rationale: An onset detector estimates pain occurrence from brain activity, complementary to rating-level prediction.
verified_result_metric: Paper reports feasibility across two EEG datasets and cross-subject/cross-modality tests versus SVM; no numeric accuracy captured in the inspected abstract/source excerpts.
prediction_target: Presence/onset of acute experimentally induced pain, not continuous subjective rating.
validation_design: Two EEG datasets with cross-subject and cross-modality evaluation; source localization and sequential modeling.
data_evidence: The primary paper links to public OSF Brain mediators of pain study data; the OSF record describes BrainVision EEG and perception-condition numeric ratings for 60 painful stimuli/condition at three intensity levels. This verifies public EEG and ratings, not that every analysis subset is identical.
relevance_limitations: Published method depends on source localization and temporal context; the linked EEG is 1000-Hz/65-channel in the cited dataset description, unlike the target 128-Hz sparse montage. Onset detection is not a pain-intensity regression target.

title: Selective and replicable neuroimaging-based indicators of pain discriminability
authors: Zhang et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Evoked-potential response amplitude and latency; pain AUC
feature_definition: Differences in N2/P2 peak amplitude and latency; signal-detection-theory AUC operationalizes an individual’s pain discriminability.
prediction_rationale: Inference: evoked EEG response features may estimate how sensitively an individual distinguishes pain intensity, not moment-to-moment pain itself.
verified_result_metric: LASSO-predicted AUC correlated with measured pain AUC: Pearson r=0.536 in Dataset 1 and r=0.423 in Dataset 2 (both p<0.0001). These are correlations, not R²/accuracy.
prediction_target: Individual pain-intensity discriminability (AUC).
validation_design: Three EEG cohorts (N=114,111,141); exploratory Dataset 1 and replication in Datasets 2/3; pain-selectivity assessed against non-pain sensory modalities.
data_evidence: Linked EEG dataset paper lists raw BIDS records including ds005292; this specific data page describes trialwise pain ratings.
relevance_limitations: Peak-based, stimulus-locked feature design requires event-aligned epochs and broad scalp electrodes; article’s AUC target is not a pain rating forecast and its evidence is not based on 5-s resting windows.

title: Chronic neuropathic pain: EEG data in eyes open and eyes closed with painDETECT and brief pain inventory reports
authors: Daniela M. Zolezzi, Norberto E. Naal-Ruiz, Luz María Alonso-Valerdi, David I. Ibarra-Zarate
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Public resting EEG resource for candidate PAC, phase connectivity and feature-stability analyses
feature_definition: Raw 250-Hz EEG from 36 chronic neuropathic-pain patients (5-min eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions) with BPI and painDETECT questionnaires; paper reports bandwidth 0.1–100 Hz.
prediction_rationale: Could test whether within-session phase/PAC summaries carry information about patient questionnaire pain scores; this is a proposed reanalysis, not a result of the data descriptor.
verified_result_metric: Not applicable (dataset item; no prediction result claimed).
prediction_target: Proposed patient-level BPI/painDETECT severity or questionnaire-defined pain features
validation_design: Dataset includes 36 patients; analyses need subject-level splits to avoid window-level leakage and independent validation before clinical claims.
data_evidence: The data article links Mendeley repository versions and identifies raw electrophysiological signals plus questionnaire/demographic files; repository metadata identifies original data and files.
relevance_limitations: Resting state, not stimulus-locked pain; only 36 patients; five-second window labels would replicate a subject’s fixed clinical scores and are not independent. Verify channel layout for network connectivity; >40-Hz analyses require changing pipeline filters, and >64-Hz content is unavailable at 250-Hz sampling.

title: EEG frequency band analysis in chronic neuropathic pain: A linear and nonlinear approach to classify pain severity
authors: Daniela M. Zolezzi; Luz María Alonso-Valerdi; David I. Ibarra-Zarate
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Approximate entropy (ApEn) and absolute EEG band power
feature_definition: ApEn (pattern-based signal irregularity) and absolute power estimated in delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma bands at 22 scalp electrodes, using one-minute segments; chronic neuropathic pain severity grouped from Brief Pain Inventory ratings.
prediction_rationale: Authors tested whether nonlinear EEG signal dynamics/strength features separate pain severity groups better than absolute band power. The result is group differentiation rather than a validated out-of-sample pain predictor.
verified_result_metric: Paper reports ApEn group differences in most bands and conditions (p <= 0.0001) and notable clustering of pain groups using theta-, alpha- and beta-band ApEn. This is inferential/group-separation evidence, not verified held-out accuracy, correlation or R².
prediction_target: Low/moderate/high chronic neuropathic pain severity from Brief Pain Inventory; no prospective prediction endpoint.
validation_design: Cross-sectional feature comparison in 36 chronic neuropathic pain participants; 13-person healthy-control EEG database used as reference. Features derived from 10 one-minute observations per patient; Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn tests and unsupervised clustering described. No independent cohort or subject-held-out predictive validation verified.
open_access_status: Open-access article page/full text at ScienceDirect; article page identifies Creative Commons access.
data_evidence: Paper states its 36-patient database is publicly available; the linked Mendeley v4 page offers a public 529 MB download with individual patient .gdf recordings, demographics/questionnaires and channel labels. The companion data descriptor confirms these are raw electrophysiological recordings (250 Hz, 22 channels) paired with BPI/painDETECT reports. The 13 control participants come from a separate database; do not imply they are all contained in Mendeley dataset yj52xrfgtz. Access-review detail: public raw EEG verified
relevance_limitations: Relevant original pain-severity EEG analysis with public raw signals and central C3/Cz/C4 leads. However, its 1-min feature segments, 250-Hz 0.1–100-Hz acquisition and broad montage differ from 5-s, 128-Hz, 1–40-Hz workflows. BPI-derived groups and within-sample clustering do not prove calibrated individual pain prediction. It shares the Zolezzi cohort with the 2024 Ryu and Barbosa papers and the 2023 dataset descriptor; cohort reuse is not independent replication.

title: Interindividual variability and individual stability of pain- and touch-related neuronal gamma oscillations
authors: E Valentini et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: pain-evoked gamma-band oscillations and within-person stability
feature_definition: Gamma response prevalence, magnitude, and repeatability following noxious pain and innocuous touch stimulation.
prediction_rationale: Characterizes whether pain-related gamma features are stable enough to function as individual biomarkers.
verified_result_metric: Paper reports marked between-person variability and individual stability in one dataset, with gamma responses evident only in a subset; no pain-rating prediction accuracy verified.
prediction_target: Pain-evoked response reproducibility/individual trait, not a validated rating predictor.
validation_design: Two EEG datasets; 48-person pain/touch dataset linked to public OSF and a repeated-session dataset; study assesses repeatability and variability.
data_evidence: Paper links the 48-participant pain/touch EEG dataset to OSF jw8rv; article methods include pain ratings. This repository is for this gamma-stability dataset, not Nickel et al. 2017 tonic heat.
relevance_limitations: Gamma frequencies above 40 Hz are removed by the target filter and most are above 64-Hz Nyquist. Gamma response variability cautions against assuming this feature is universal.

title: Pain- and touch-related neuronal gamma oscillation EEG dataset (OSF jw8rv)
authors: E Valentini et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: raw EEG, pain/touch event-related gamma, trial ratings
feature_definition: Public 48-participant EEG dataset with painful laser and matched tactile trials; paper also reports a separate repeated-session dataset.
prediction_rationale: Enables analysis of gamma response variability, stability, and relation to single-trial pain ratings.
verified_result_metric: Publicly linked dataset contains 48 healthy participants; 75 laser-pain and 75 touch trials, ratings 0–10 after each; no dataset prediction metric.
prediction_target: Pain/touch intensity ratings and event-related gamma response features.
validation_design: Single-session dataset of 48 participants; the linked study also discusses a distinct two-session 22-person dataset, do not assume both are in this OSF record.
open_access_status: Public OSF project; article open access
data_evidence: Valentini et al. explicitly link jw8rv and describe its 48 healthy participants, pain/touch paradigms, and ratings. This is distinct from Nickel et al. 2017 tonic-heat data.
relevance_limitations: Gamma above 40 Hz is removed by target filter; 64-Hz Nyquist prevents higher components. Pain and touch blocks, trial events, full montage and sampling must be checked; only C3/C4/Cz remain in target pipeline.

title: 1/f in chronic pain: raw EEG datasets linked to the preregistered aperiodic analysis
authors: Cristina Gil Ávila; Markus Ploner; linked cohort contributors
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Resting-state raw BIDS EEG with clinical pain labels; source data for periodic/aperiodic and alpha analyses
feature_definition: Public OSF project joins/references raw EEG cohorts; preregistration identifies eyes-open/closed five-minute resting state recordings and pain ratings.
prediction_rationale: Raw EEG tied to pain intensity and case/control labels permits reproducible spectral-power and aperiodic feature tests; no standalone prediction is claimed for this repository.
verified_result_metric: Dataset item; no model metric applies.
prediction_target: Cohort diagnosis and pain intensity labels linked to EEG; not a model result.
validation_design: Public multi-cohort dataset resource; study article analyzed 149 pain participants and 115 controls; source cohort count and inclusion rules differ.
open_access_status: Public OSF projects; preregistration states there are no dataset access restrictions.
data_evidence: OSF qgfma is public and links the raw-data cohort projects; preregistration xshmy explicitly lists raw BIDS-EEG URLs srpbg, a8bpx and qgfma, states public/no restrictions, and ties them to this chronic-pain study. The fetched srpbg/a8bpx OSF pages are Public Projects with study-identifying records and raw-data components/folders (their folder listings show 0 B; file bytes were not independently downloaded).
relevance_limitations: 64-channel raw BIDS EEG, 1000 Hz original sampling; original paper uses eyes-closed five-minute sessions, source reconstruction and mPFC. Requires montage mapping, preprocessing, timing and baseline audit. Only C3/C4/Cz and five-second 1–40 Hz model cannot reproduce source-localized frontal alpha/aperiodic analysis.

title: Resting-state electroencephalography delta and theta bands as compensatory oscillations in chronic neuropathic pain: a secondary data analysis
authors: Sara Pinto Barbosa; Ygor Nascimento Junqueira; Milena Apetito Akamatsu; Lucas Murrins Marques; Adriano Teixeira; Matheus Lobo; Mohamed H Mahmoud; Walid E Omer; Kevin Pacheco-Barrios; Felipe Fregni
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Relative EEG band power (delta, theta, alpha, beta and sub-bands)
feature_definition: Resting eyes-closed relative power calculated with FFT from 5-second windows with 50% overlap; regional central, frontal and parietal power features analyzed against BPI pain intensity and interference outcomes.
prediction_rationale: The secondary analysis asks whether resting EEG spectral signal strength relates to pain severity/interference in neuropathic pain. Findings are associations from a small cross-sectional sample, not a validated forecast.
verified_result_metric: Authors report no significant multivariate model for pain during EEG or most interference outcomes; the model for average pain intensity over the prior four weeks and a separate mood-interference model were significant. Authors describe central alpha as associated with higher pain and central delta with lower pain. No independent-validation performance metric was verified.
prediction_target: Average pain intensity in the previous four weeks and BPI pain-interference outcomes; pain during EEG was also analyzed.
validation_design: Secondary cross-sectional analysis of 36 chronic neuropathic-pain participants from Zolezzi et al. 2023. Linear/logistic regression with age and medication consideration; most nonnormal pain/interference outcomes were dichotomized at the median. No independent test sample/external validation.
data_evidence: The article identifies the sample as the public Zolezzi 2023 dataset, states the used data were provided by the original authors and are available in a publicly accessible database, and uses 36 patient EEG/BPI records. Mendeley v4 provides raw patient .gdf EEG and questionnaire files. Same participant cohort as Zolezzi 2023 and Ryu 2024; not a new cohort. Access-review detail: public raw EEG verified
relevance_limitations: The paper uses 5-s windows, but these are overlapping derived observations from 36 participants with person-level pain questionnaires; window count does not create independent participants. Its 250-Hz recordings, broad montage and five-minute eyes-closed state differ from three-central-channel recordings. Association and regression are not held-out prediction; regional results and outcome coding need replication.

title: Resting-state frontal electroencephalography (EEG) biomarkers for detecting the severity of chronic neuropathic pain
authors: S. Ryu, D. Gwon, C. Park, Y. Ha, M. Ahn
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Frontal EEG PAC and PAC asymmetry; spectral power asymmetry
feature_definition: Cross-frequency coupling between low-frequency phase and higher-frequency amplitude at Fp1/Fp2; left-right asymmetry features.
prediction_rationale: PAC/asymmetry may capture chronic pain severity-related nonstationary interactions missed by band power; this rationale is directly tested by the paper’s correlations and regression models.
verified_result_metric: Reported r: beta-power asymmetry −0.375; gamma-power asymmetry −0.433; low-beta-to-low-gamma coupling −0.397. Best polynomial-kernel SVR R²=0.655; no external validation verified.
prediction_target: Patient-level chronic neuropathic pain intensity from clinical ratings
validation_design: Secondary analysis of public resting EEG from 36 patients; feature-score correlations and five-model regression comparison; no external cohort/independent-site validation reported in retrieved abstract.
data_evidence: Ryu methods explicitly identify a publicly available dataset from the cited Zolezzi study; the linked 2023 data paper reports raw resting EEG plus BPI/painDETECT reports and Mendeley repository DOI 10.17632/yj52xrfgtz.4.
relevance_limitations: The actual predictor channels are Fp1/Fp2, absent in C3/C4/Cz pipeline; frontal asymmetry cannot be recreated. Resting 5-min eyes-open data and person-level pain labels differ from five-second trial labels. Gamma feature bands may exceed 40 Hz; any >64-Hz high-gamma component is beyond 128-Hz Nyquist and current filter.

title: A comprehensive EEG dataset of laser-evoked potentials for pain research
authors: X Zhao, J Zhou, L Zhang, Y Zhuang, H Duan, S Wei, S Yao, X Lu, Y Bi, L Hu
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: high-density LEP, raw EEG and trial pain ratings
feature_definition: Dataset paper describing single-trial LEP EEG and ratings for graded laser stimuli.
prediction_rationale: Large dataset enables within- and between-person LEP feature analysis/prediction, though the paper is a resource description rather than a prediction model.
verified_result_metric: 678 healthy participants; the paper describes raw high-density EEG, 2.5–4.5-J laser stimuli, and single-trial pain ratings; no model prediction metric claimed.
prediction_target: Resource for future prediction of single-trial subjective pain rating; no predictor evaluated.
validation_design: Large-scale data resource with technical validation of EEG responses and stimulus-intensity/rating trends.
data_evidence: Paper's Data Records section explicitly lists nine OpenNeuro BIDS datasets (ds005284, ds005285, ds005289, ds005286, ds005291, ds005293, ds005292, ds005280, ds005473); raw EEG plus per-trial stimulus and subjective pain ratings in EEGLAB epoch structures; preprocessed data/code also linked.
relevance_limitations: High-density resource, but recording systems/sampling rates differ by experiment; inspect each dataset's EEG JSON. Event-locked LEPs require markers/epochs; do not presume all data meet 128 Hz or C3/C4/Cz without harmonization.

title: Assessing the balance between excitation and inhibition in chronic pain through the aperiodic component of EEG
authors: Cristina Gil Ávila; Elisabeth S. May; Felix S. Bott; Laura Tiemann; Vanessa Hohn; Henrik Heitmann; Paul Theo Zebhauser; Joachim Gross; Markus Ploner
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Aperiodic exponent (aperiodic 1/f slope) and periodic/aperiodic spectral separation
feature_definition: Fit the 2–40 Hz power spectrum into aperiodic offset/exponent plus oscillatory peaks; primary feature was exponent in source-localized mPFC, with whole-brain analyses.
prediction_rationale: Aperiodic exponent was proposed as a scalable proxy for excitation/inhibition and a candidate marker of chronic pain; this study provides strong counter-evidence to simple status/intensity prediction.
verified_result_metric: Authors report robust evidence against chronic-pain/control exponent differences (all BF10 <0.22 across preregistered analyses); no relationship with pain intensity. Not classification accuracy or R².
prediction_target: Chronic pain vs healthy status and average pain intensity association; no deployed or validated predictor.
validation_design: Preregistered secondary analysis of 3 EEG cohorts; blinded analyses and multiverse; 149 chronic pain and 115 controls in final sample.
open_access_status: Open access; full article freely readable at eLife.
data_evidence: Paper reports a third cohort made public; OSF qgfma is public and links raw-data projects for Ta Dinh 2019 (g3snh) and Heitmann 2022 (gywtc). The linked preregistration states no access restrictions and identifies raw BIDS EEG URLs srpbg, a8bpx and qgfma. Data access is verified at OSF project level; cohort composition differs from final analyzed N.
relevance_limitations: Scalp EEG has 64 channels, 1000 Hz acquisition and 5-minute eyes-closed recordings before preprocessing; main mPFC/source analyses cannot be replicated with C3/C4/Cz alone. 2–40 Hz fitting is compatible with 1–40 Hz filter, but 5-second windows do not reproduce full source/aperiodic pipeline. No alpha asymmetry test.

title: Assessing the predictive value of peak alpha frequency for the sensitivity to pain
authors: E S May, L Tiemann, C Gil Ávila, F S Bott, V D Hohn, J Gross, M Ploner
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: resting-state peak alpha frequency (PAF)
feature_definition: Peak frequency in the alpha range (8–13 Hz) in resting EEG, related to interindividual and intraindividual pain ratings during brief laser pain.
prediction_rationale: Evaluates whether previously proposed resting PAF biomarker generalizes to brief experimental pain.
verified_result_metric: 159 healthy participants, two sessions; multiverse/specification-curve analyses did not yield consistent evidence that PAF predicts sensitivity to brief laser pain.
prediction_target: Between-person and within-person pain sensitivity from brief laser stimuli.
validation_design: Two identical sessions with replication across sessions; 159 participants.
data_evidence: Paper data statement explicitly says raw and preprocessed EEG-BIDS and analysis code are openly available at OSF s75q6.
relevance_limitations: Resting PAF needs a sufficiently long clean resting segment; a single five-second window may be unstable. Within 1–40 Hz and Nyquist, but central-only montage may omit optimal sensorimotor locations.

feature_family: raw BrainVision EEG, nociceptive stimulation, verbal ratings
feature_definition: Public EEG project with perception condition: 60 painful laser trials at three individualized intensity levels, numeric pain report after each stimulus; also motor/autonomic conditions.
prediction_rationale: Public perception condition provides signal aligned to numeric pain labels, while ancillary motor and autonomic channels/conditions can support multimodal analyses.
verified_result_metric: OSF record verifies public BrainVision EEG and 60-trial design; this is dataset metadata rather than predictor performance.
prediction_target: Numeric pain rating (0–100) per trial in perception task.

data_evidence: OSF primary page states project is public, lists raw .eeg/.vhdr/.vmrk files and numeric-rating perception condition; Sun et al. 2020 primary paper links to this dataset.
relevance_limitations: The repository is BrainVision format and channel/sample details must be checked from headers; published onset-detection target is not the same as pain intensity prediction. Harmonize sampling and montage first.

title: Test-retest reliability of spectral parameterization by 1/f characterization using SpecParam
authors: Daniel J. McKeown, Anna J. Finley, Nicholas J. Kelley, James F. Cavanagh, Hannah A. D. Keage, Oliver Baumann, Victor R. Schinazi, Ahmed A. Moustafa, and Douglas J. Angus
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Test-retest reliability of periodic and aperiodic spectral power features
feature_definition: SpecParam/FOOOF parameterization of EEG spectra into periodic peak parameters (power, central frequency, bandwidth) and aperiodic exponent/offset; repeated across resting eyes-open/eyes-closed and cognitive task recordings.
prediction_rationale: Inference: a feature family with measurable within-person test-retest stability provides a baseline for expected feature noise and repeatability; this is reliability evidence, not evidence that the feature detects pain or preserves amplitude under denoising.
verified_result_metric: Full-text qualitative result extracted: aperiodic exponent and offset were generally reliable; parameterized alpha/beta activity was more reliable than theta, with eyes-open fitting/data-loss limitations. Numeric metrics not copied into this record.
prediction_target: Test-retest reliability of EEG periodic/aperiodic spectral parameters; no pain prediction target.
validation_design: Secondary analysis of the publicly released 60-person repeated-session OpenNeuro cohort; the paper's analyzed sample was 49 healthy young adults across three sessions (two same-day sessions and a session about one month later), with rest and three cognitive tasks.
data_evidence: The paper's Data availability section identifies OpenNeuro ds004148 as its original 60-person cohort. OpenNeuro landing page reports 64-channel, 500-Hz recordings and participant files; this is actual recorded EEG, separate from the paper's derived spectral parameters. Access-review detail: Public EEG recordings verified on OpenNeuro; article explicitly identifies the original 60-person dataset. The repository contains BIDS EEG files; this record does not claim the derived SpecParam features themselves are raw EEG.
relevance_limitations: Healthy young adults and resting/cognitive states only; it evaluates spectral reliability, not pain, blink artifact removal, or the reliability of short 5-s C3/C4/Cz time-domain variance. Does not establish pain specificity.

title: Test-Retest Reliability of Single Spectral Power and Spectral Power Ratios in Relative and Absolute Values
authors: Jinwon Chang
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Absolute/relative band power and band-power ratios; test-retest ICC
feature_definition: FFT-derived absolute and relative single-band power and spectral power ratios computed across five scalp regions; alpha/beta ratio singled out for reliability comparison.
prediction_rationale: Inference: ratios may provide more repeatable strength features across sessions than absolute or relative single-band power, motivating reliability-first evaluation before clinical or pain prediction; not a denoising result.
verified_result_metric: Full text reports absolute alpha/beta ratios in central, parietal, occipital, and temporal regions with ICC > 0.75 in both datasets; the article reports the direction as more reliable than single-band absolute/relative power.
prediction_target: Short- and long-term reproducibility of EEG spectral-power features, not pain ratings or pain classification.
validation_design: Two independent healthy-adult datasets: Dataset 1, 60 people across three sessions (two same day, one month later); Dataset 2, 74 people with sessions one hour apart. Repeated-measures reliability assessed using ICCs. Dataset 1 overlaps the publicly released ds004148 cohort used by the SpecParam paper; Dataset 2 is an additional OpenNeuro cohort.
data_evidence: Full paper names OpenNeuro ds004148 and ds003478 in its Data Availability Statement. OpenNeuro pages expose participant-level EEG BIDS files. The ds003478 README explicitly notes that some channels were interpolated and there are no raw data to revert to; thus the dataset is public EEG but includes processing caveats. Access-review detail: Public OpenNeuro EEG datasets verified by the paper's Data Availability Statement. ds004148 provides the repeated-state 60-person EEG cohort; ds003478 provides EEG records but its README notes some channel interpolation and that raw pre-interpolation data are unavailable, so not all data are pristine original acquisition files.
relevance_limitations: Transferable repeatability evidence only: no pain labels, no pain-validation cohort, and no denoising intervention. Ratio-based spectral features differ from time-domain variance and may not transfer to low-density central-channel pain analyses. Dataset 1 overlaps a cohort in the SpecParam study; Dataset 2 adds a distinct repository/cohort.
